instructions: Open book. Answer each item from the saved AWS pages and the fact canon only. Give citations for every label: why the key is right and why each other option is wrong. A citation is a fact id or {source_id, quote} with a verbatim quote. Set flag when a second answer is defensible, else null.

items.stem: A company runs a photo-sharing mobile app. The app's backend runs on Amazon EC2 instances that use an IAM role. Users must upload photos from the app directly to a private Amazon S3 bucket, without sending the photos through the backend. The users do not have AWS credentials. Each upload must be allowed for a short, temporary period. Which solution will allow the uploads in the MOST secure way?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an IAM user that can call s3:PutObject on the bucket, and store the user's access key in the app to sign each upload.

options.label: B
options.text: Let a developer presign upload URLs with the longest expiry from the developer's IAM user, and ship the URLs inside the app.

options.label: C
options.text: Have the backend use its IAM role to presign a URL for one object key with a short expiry, and return the URL to the app.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a bucket policy that allows s3:PutObject for every principal on an uploads prefix, and turn off Block Public Access for the bucket.

items.stem: A company turned on S3 Cross-Region Replication from a bucket in one AWS Region to a bucket in a second Region. Versioning is turned on for both buckets. The source bucket already held 2 years of objects when the replication rule was created. New objects now appear in the destination bucket, but the older objects do not. The company must replicate the older objects too. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Write a script that lists every object in the source bucket and copies each object to the destination bucket with the AWS CLI.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an S3 Batch Replication job for the replication rule, so that S3 replicates the objects that existed before the rule was created.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on S3 Replication Time Control for the replication rule, so that S3 replicates the older objects to the destination within a set time.

options.label: D
options.text: Suspend versioning on the destination bucket and turn it on again, so that the replication rule starts again for all objects.

items.stem: A company has 200 Amazon S3 buckets in one AWS account. Developers sometimes add bucket policies that allow public reads, and the security team finds them weeks later. Only the security team can change account-level settings. The company must ensure that no bucket in the account can be made public by a bucket policy, now or in the future. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on all four S3 Block Public Access settings on each bucket, and turn them on for each new bucket after it is created.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an AWS Config rule that checks each bucket policy for public access, and report the noncompliant buckets to the security team.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on all four S3 Block Public Access settings at the account level, so that the settings apply to every bucket in the account.

options.label: D
options.text: Turn on IAM Access Analyzer for S3, and send an alert to the security team when a bucket policy allows public access.

items.stem: A research team creates data files of about 2 TB each in its data center. The team must store each file as one object in an Amazon S3 bucket. The team uploads the files with the AWS CLI over an internet connection that sometimes drops. When the connection drops, the team must not have to send the whole file again. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Upload each file through the Amazon S3 console in a browser, which shows the progress of each file during the upload.

options.label: B
options.text: Upload each file with multipart upload, so that the parts travel in parallel and a failed part is sent again on its own.

options.label: C
options.text: Upload each file with one PUT request, and set a long timeout in the AWS CLI so that the large request can finish.

options.label: D
options.text: Split each file into objects of 5 GB, and upload each object with one PUT request to the same bucket prefix.

items.stem: A company stores customer contracts in an Amazon S3 bucket and relies on the durability of Amazon S3 to protect them. Last month, an employee deleted several contracts by mistake, and another employee overwrote a contract with the wrong file. The company could not recover any of them. The company must be able to recover from accidental deletes and overwrites in the future. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Make no change to the bucket, because S3 durability already keeps several copies of every object across Availability Zones.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a bucket policy that denies the s3:DeleteObject action to every principal in the account, except the security team.

options.label: C
options.text: Run a nightly script that copies every object in the bucket to a second bucket in another AWS Region for recovery.

options.label: D
options.text: Turn on S3 Versioning for the bucket, and add a lifecycle rule that expires noncurrent versions after a set number of days.

items.stem: A company runs a video editing service. Users around the world upload project files of 2 GB to 20 GB to one Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. Users who are far from the Region report slow uploads that do not use their full bandwidth. The company wants faster uploads to the same bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a bucket in a Region near each group of users, and replicate each bucket to the us-east-1 bucket with Cross-Region Replication.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on S3 Transfer Acceleration for the bucket, and change the upload clients to use the accelerate endpoint of the bucket.

options.label: C
options.text: Order an AWS Direct Connect connection from each user location to the us-east-1 Region, and send the uploads over those connections.

options.label: D
options.text: Change the upload clients to send each file in one PUT request instead of many parts, to cut the number of round trips.

items.stem: A financial services company stores trade records as objects in a new Amazon S3 bucket. An application uploads thousands of records each day. The company must retain each record in an immutable form for 7 years. No user, including the root user, can be allowed to delete or overwrite a record before the end of its retention period. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on S3 Object Lock for the bucket in compliance mode, and set a default retention period of 7 years that applies to every new object version.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on S3 Object Lock for the bucket, and change the application so that every upload request sets compliance mode and a retain-until date 7 years ahead.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on S3 Object Lock for the bucket in governance mode, set a default retention period of 7 years, and allow only the security team to bypass governance retention.

options.label: D
options.text: Turn on S3 Object Lock for the bucket, change the application so that every upload sets governance mode and a 7-year retain-until date, and let only the security team bypass it.

items.stem: A company stores signed contracts as objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company manages its own keys in a hardware security module in its data center. Company policy says that the encryption keys must never be stored in AWS. Amazon S3 must encrypt each object at rest and decrypt it when an authorized user downloads it. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on SSE-C for the bucket, and send the company's key over HTTPS with every upload request and every download request.

options.label: B
options.text: Use SSE-KMS with a customer managed key in AWS KMS, and let the company's security team control the key policy and the key rotation.

options.label: C
options.text: Encrypt each object in the data center before upload, and also turn on SSE-C and send the company's key with every request.

options.label: D
options.text: Encrypt each object in the data center with the company's key before upload, and decrypt it in the data center after download.

items.stem: A company stores daily sales exports in an Amazon S3 bucket in account A. ACLs are disabled on the bucket, and the objects are encrypted with SSE-S3. A reporting application runs as an AWS Lambda function in account B and uses an execution role. The application must read the exports, and the security team requires least privilege. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST securely? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Add a statement to the bucket policy in account A that allows s3:GetObject for the wildcard principal when the user agent names account B.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a statement to the bucket policy in account A that allows s3:GetObject on the export objects for the ARN of the execution role.

options.label: C
options.text: Add the canonical user ID of account B to the ACL of each export object with read permission, and leave the bucket policy unchanged.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an IAM user in account A with read access to the bucket, and store the access key of the user in an environment variable of the function.

options.label: E
options.text: Add a statement to the identity-based policy of the execution role in account B that allows s3:GetObject on the export objects.

items.stem: A company receives order files from partners in an Amazon S3 bucket. Each new file must start a processing job. The processing team runs workers that read from an existing Amazon SQS FIFO queue, and the team will not change the workers. The company wants to decouple the upload side from the processing side and does not need S3 to keep events in order. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.label: A
options.text: Write an AWS Lambda function that lists the bucket every minute, finds the new files, and sends a message to the SQS FIFO queue for each one.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on Amazon EventBridge delivery for the bucket, and create an EventBridge rule that matches object-created events and targets the SQS FIFO queue.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function, and write code in the function that sends each event to the SQS FIFO queue.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure an S3 event notification for object-created events that sends each event directly to the SQS FIFO queue as its destination.

items.stem: Several application teams in one AWS account read a shared dataset in one Amazon S3 bucket. The bucket policy is close to its size limit, and it already delegates access control to the access points of the account. A new analytics team must read the dataset privately from its own VPC, which has a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3. The company must restrict the analytics team's access to that VPC. Access for the other teams, including their console use, must not change. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Copy the dataset to a second bucket with S3 Replication, and give the second bucket a policy that allows reads only through the analytics VPC endpoint.

options.label: B
options.text: Attach a security group to the bucket that allows inbound HTTPS requests only from the CIDR range of the analytics VPC, and keep the bucket policy unchanged.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an S3 access point with a VPC network origin for the analytics VPC, and give it a policy that allows the analytics team's role to read.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a statement to the bucket policy that denies every request that does not arrive through the analytics VPC endpoint, by using the aws:SourceVpce condition key.

items.stem: A company stores product images in an Amazon S3 bucket. Each image is larger than 1 MB. The images are infrequently accessed: a user opens each image about once a month. When a user opens an image, the image must load in milliseconds. The images are thumbnails that the company can generate again from the original files at any time. Which storage class is the MOST cost-effective choice that meets these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Store the images in S3 One Zone-IA, which stores data in a single Availability Zone and charges a per-GB retrieval fee.

options.label: B
options.text: Store the images in S3 Standard-IA, which stores data across multiple Availability Zones and charges a per-GB retrieval fee.

options.label: C
options.text: Store the images in S3 Glacier Deep Archive, which has the lowest storage price of all the S3 storage classes.

options.label: D
options.text: Store the images in S3 Standard, which stores data across multiple Availability Zones and charges no retrieval fee.

items.stem: A company stores application logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Each log file is larger than 1 MB, and the bucket holds the only copy. Engineers read the logs often for 30 days and rarely from day 30 to day 90, when a log must still open in milliseconds. After 90 days, the logs are an archive: auditors read a few logs each year and can wait up to 12 hours. The company must retain the logs for 7 years and then delete them. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Add one lifecycle rule that transitions the logs to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days, and expires them after 7 years.

options.label: B
options.text: Add one lifecycle rule that transitions the logs to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days, and moves a log back to S3 Standard when an auditor asks for it.

options.label: C
options.text: Add one lifecycle rule that transitions the logs to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days, and expires them after 7 years.

options.label: D
options.text: Add one lifecycle rule that transitions the logs to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and to S3 One Zone-IA after 90 days, and expires them after 7 years.

items.stem: A research institute stores a large genomics dataset in an Amazon S3 bucket. Partner organizations download parts of the dataset into their own AWS accounts in several AWS Regions. The institute's bill for requests and data transfer grows every month because of these downloads. The institute wants to avoid paying for the partners' requests and downloads, and the partners agree to pay for them. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Generate presigned URLs with the institute's IAM role for the objects that each partner needs, and send the URLs to the partners.

options.label: B
options.text: Replicate the dataset with S3 Cross-Region Replication to a bucket in each partner's account in the partner's Region.

options.label: C
options.text: Move the dataset to S3 Intelligent-Tiering, so that the cost of the partners' downloads goes down as access patterns change.

options.label: D
options.text: Turn on Requester Pays for the bucket, and allow the partner accounts to read the dataset in the bucket policy.

items.stem: A company runs a batch job once a day that writes about 1 million JSON result files to an Amazon S3 bucket in S3 Standard. Each file is about 20 KB. An analytics job reads all the results of one day together. After the first week, the results are infrequently accessed, about once a month, and each read must return data in milliseconds. The company wants to lower the storage cost of results that are older than 30 days. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Add a lifecycle rule that moves each 20 KB result file to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days, which has the lowest storage price.

options.label: B
options.text: Combine each day's results into one large object before upload, and add a lifecycle rule that moves these objects to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days.

options.label: C
options.text: Add a lifecycle rule that moves each 20 KB result file to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 30 days, so that unread files move to cheaper tiers.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a lifecycle rule that moves each 20 KB result file to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days, with an object size filter that includes the small files.

items.stem: A company stores product images in an Amazon S3 bucket. Each image is larger than 1 MB. The images are infrequently accessed: a user opens each image about once a month. When a user opens an image, the image must load in milliseconds. The images are the only copy, and they must remain available if an Availability Zone is lost. Which storage class is the MOST cost-effective choice that meets these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Store the images in S3 One Zone-IA, which stores data in a single Availability Zone and charges a per-GB retrieval fee.

options.label: B
options.text: Store the images in S3 Standard, which stores data across multiple Availability Zones and charges no retrieval fee.

options.label: C
options.text: Store the images in S3 Glacier Deep Archive, which has the lowest storage price of all the S3 storage classes.

options.label: D
options.text: Store the images in S3 Standard-IA, which stores data across multiple Availability Zones and charges a per-GB retrieval fee.

items.stem: A company runs a media library in an Amazon S3 bucket. The bucket is the only copy of the files, and each file is larger than 10 MB. Some files are read many times each day for months. Other files are never read after their first week. Nobody can predict which files will stay popular, so the access pattern of each file is unpredictable. Which storage approach is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Store the files in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, and serve each file to users with a normal GET request when they ask for it.

options.label: B
options.text: Store the files in S3 One Zone-IA, because it costs less than S3 Standard-IA and keeps the same eleven nines of durability.

options.label: C
options.text: Store the files in S3 Intelligent-Tiering, so that S3 moves each file between access tiers based on how often the file is read.

options.label: D
options.text: Store the files in S3 Standard, and add a lifecycle rule that moves every file to S3 Standard-IA 30 days after upload.

items.stem: A company must keep recordings of customer calls for 10 years to meet a legal rule. The recordings are audio files of 20 MB to 200 MB each, and nobody reads them during normal operations. About twice a year, auditors ask for a few recordings. A wait of up to 48 hours for those recordings is acceptable. The company wants to archive the recordings in Amazon S3. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Store the recordings in S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, and read each requested recording directly with a GET request when the auditors ask.

options.label: B
options.text: Store the recordings in S3 Standard-IA, and read each requested recording directly with a GET request when the auditors ask.

options.label: C
options.text: Store the recordings in S3 Glacier Deep Archive, and restore each requested recording with the Bulk retrieval option when the auditors ask.

options.label: D
options.text: Store the recordings in S3 Glacier Deep Archive, and restore each requested recording with the Expedited retrieval option when the auditors ask.

items.stem: A financial services company stores trade records as objects in a new Amazon S3 bucket. An application uploads thousands of records each day. The company must retain each record in an immutable form for 7 years. Most users must not be able to delete or overwrite a record, but the security team must be able to remove the protection when a legal request requires it. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on S3 Object Lock for the bucket, and change the application so that every upload request sets compliance mode and a retain-until date 7 years ahead.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on S3 Object Lock for the bucket, change the application so that every upload sets governance mode and a 7-year retain-until date, and let only the security team bypass it.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on S3 Object Lock for the bucket in compliance mode, and set a default retention period of 7 years that applies to every new object version.

options.label: D
options.text: Turn on S3 Object Lock for the bucket in governance mode, set a default retention period of 7 years, and allow only the security team to bypass governance retention.

items.stem: A company stores signed contracts as objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company manages its own keys in a hardware security module in its data center. Company policy says that the encryption keys must never be stored in AWS. Each object must be encrypted before it leaves the data center, so that AWS never sees unencrypted data in transit or at rest. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.label: A
options.text: Encrypt each object in the data center with the company's key before upload, and decrypt it in the data center after download.

options.label: B
options.text: Encrypt each object in the data center before upload, and also turn on SSE-C and send the company's key with every request.

options.label: C
options.text: Use SSE-KMS with a customer managed key in AWS KMS, and let the company's security team control the key policy and the key rotation.

options.label: D
options.text: Turn on SSE-C for the bucket, and send the company's key over HTTPS with every upload request and every download request.

items.stem: A hospital group stores medical images in Amazon S3. Each image is between 5 MB and 50 MB, and the images must be kept for many years. Doctors open a given image about once a quarter. When a doctor opens an image, the image must load in real time, within milliseconds. The hospital group wants to reduce its storage costs. Which storage class is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, with each image read directly by a normal GET request each time a doctor opens it.

options.label: B
options.text: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, with an Expedited retrieval request sent each time a doctor opens one of the images.

options.label: C
options.text: S3 Standard-IA, with each image read directly by a normal GET request each time a doctor opens one of the images.

options.label: D
options.text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering with the Deep Archive Access tier turned on, with each image read by a normal GET request.

items.stem: A company stores build artifacts in an Amazon S3 bucket that has S3 Versioning turned on. The number of current objects stays about the same each month, but the storage bill grows every month. Most of the stored bytes belong to noncurrent object versions. S3 Storage Lens also shows that the bucket has no lifecycle rule to abort incomplete multipart uploads. The company needs every current version and wants to keep old versions for 30 days. Which combination of steps is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Add a lifecycle rule with an Expiration action for current object versions, so that S3 also removes the parts of incomplete multipart uploads.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a lifecycle rule with the AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload action that stops uploads that are not complete 7 days after they start.

options.label: C
options.text: Suspend S3 Versioning on the bucket, so that S3 removes the noncurrent object versions that the bucket already stores.

options.label: D
options.text: Add a lifecycle rule that moves noncurrent object versions to S3 Glacier Deep Archive 30 days after they become noncurrent.

options.label: E
options.text: Add a lifecycle rule with the NoncurrentVersionExpiration action that permanently deletes object versions 30 days after they become noncurrent.
